=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:27572-27580 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: In `_security_audit_tracker_stall_guard`, when `gh issue edit` fails the log line still reports `removed=<attempted labels>` (google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite says it also prints `outcome=cleaned`), so the log is misleading.
  WHY: Operators or log parsers may conclude the labels were removed when they were not, which contradicts the `removed=<comma-list|none>` contract. The fix is to set `removed="none"` in the failure branch. Reviewers disagree on the outcome value logged. All rate it NIT.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:26957 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: A ShellCheck failure is attributed to this change. google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite and openai_gpt-6-luna point to `is_truthy ... && echo true || echo false` (SC2015) on line 26957. z-ai_glm-5_3-flash says SC2015 does not hold and the failing rule is unidentified, with the diagnostic somewhere in the four new hunks (lines 306-316, 26956-26957, 27547-27582, 27636-27660).
  WHY: The pre-push gate lists `shellcheck` as a change-caused failure, which would block CI. Severities differ: BLOCKER from google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite and MAJOR from openai_gpt-6-luna and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash, so the highest is used. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 rejected this finding: SC2015 is info-level, CI uses `--severity=error`, and the same pattern already exists at lines 9246 and 9487.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:27547-27582 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `_security_audit_tracker_stall_guard` strips `ai:blocked` and the phase labels from any issue carrying `ai:security-audit`, without checking the `<!-- ai:security-audit-tracker:v1 -->` body marker or the author. The reviewer raised this under both the security and trust-boundary lenses.
  WHY: A member with triage rights could craft a tracker-shaped issue and have the poller act on it, though the threat model is bounded. Rated NIT.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:_sat_discovery_labels fold-in in run_standalone_stall_recovery and the guard call at the candidate loop | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5]
  PROBLEM: Every open `ai:security-audit` issue is now a candidate on every tick, and each clean tracker emits `STALL_RECOVERY_SKIP ... removed=none outcome=clean`.
  WHY: Nothing breaks; it adds one candidate to the existing batch and one log line per tick. Rated NIT.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "The PR must use `Refs #3576`, not an auto-close keyword."
  expected_change_site: PR description (PR body)
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  EVIDENCE: The PR description reads "Closes https://github.com/shubhodeep1/coding-workflows/issues/3576", which would auto-close tracker #3576 on merge. `scripts/lint_pr_body_auto_close.py` only checks `ai:orchestrator-tracking` issues, so it does not catch this. Severity is BLOCKER from four reviewers and MAJOR from anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5.
- requirement: Kill-switch operability: "false restores current behavior". `SECURITY_AUDIT_TRACKER_PIPELINE_EXCLUDE_ENABLED` should be forwardable from a repository variable to the poller environment.
  expected_change_site: .github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml and workflow-templates/ai-orchestrate-poll.yml
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5]
  EVIDENCE: No workflow YAML maps a `vars.*` value to the env var, so a repository variable set to false does nothing. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 notes the grant excludes workflow files, the fragment and changelog say the switch is poller-environment only, and it did not count this as a gap (NIT). google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite and minimax_minimax-m3 rated it MAJOR.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

  PROBLEM: `removed` is set to the attempted labels before `gh_retry gh issue edit` runs, so a failed edit still logs `removed=ai:blocked,...` next to `outcome=remove_failed`.
  WHY: The log shows labels as removed that are still on the tracker, contradicting the `removed=<comma-list|none>` contract in `agents.d/3576-security-audit-tracker-pipeline-exclude.md`. Only the log is wrong. Fix: set `removed="none"` in the `else` branch.

  WHY: Nothing breaks; it is one extra candidate in the existing batch and one log line per tick, as documented.

- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:27547-27582 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The guard strips `ai:blocked` and phase labels from any issue carrying `ai:security-audit` without verifying the `<!-- ai:security-audit-tracker:v1 -->` marker or the issue author.
  WHY: The guard is keyed on the label name alone, so a crafted tracker-shaped issue is treated like the real one.

  PROBLEM: On the `remove_failed` branch the log still emits `removed=ai:blocked,ai:clarification` (the targeted labels) alongside `outcome=remove_failed`.
  WHY: The `removed` field reads as past tense and the `::warning::` is easy to miss, so operators may conclude the removal succeeded.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:27573 (guard called from line 27771 in run_standalone_stall_recovery) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The guard fires `gh issue edit` label writes based only on the `ai:security-audit` label, with no marker check and no author or login verification.
  WHY: Adding the label needs write or triage rights, so the threat model is bounded, but a repo member could impersonate a tracker issue and have the poller strip its labels.
